post.description:
Reconciles staged changes with the database using routing logic.

This endpoint processes all staged changes and reconciles them into the database state:
- Analyzes staged modules, links, properties, and metadata
- Uses routing logic to discover signal paths
- Generates usecases that represent the discovered paths
- Creates/updates/deletes usecases to match the reconciled state
- Persists all changes to the database

The reconciliation process ensures the database state accurately reflects the staged modifications.

This operation is idempotent - multiple invocations produce the same result.
If no staged changes exist, returns empty arrays with success: true.

Note: warnings and errors arrays are placeholders and will be populated when the validation framework is introduced.

Start a new session with specified mode. Returns error if a session is already active.

### READONLY
- Only read APIs are supported

### TUNING

### DESIGNER
- Read APIs

- Designer APIs (add-module, add-data-link, etc.)

- Read APIs

**Important**: If an invalid API is called during a session, it will return `403 Forbidden` with error code `INVALID_OPERATION_FOR_MODE`.

Returns array of usecases with raw GKV (Graph Key-Value) information.

**Response Structure:**
Each response item contains:
- `usecases`: Array containing a single UsecaseIdentifierDto with complete raw GKV

**For subsystem-filtered usecases:**
- Use the `/usecases/filtered-by-subsystem` endpoint instead

**Optional Filtering:**
You can optionally filter usecases using the `filter` query parameter. The filter supports:
- `spfModuleInstanceId`: Filter by SPF module natural instance IDs
- `subgraphId`: Filter by subgraph system IDs
- `containerId`: Filter by container system IDs
- Operators: Use `AND`, `OR`, and parentheses for complex filtering

See the filter parameter documentation for detailed examples and usage.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Filter expression to filter usecases. Supports natural query syntax with explicit operators.

**Syntax:**
- Single condition: `field:value`
- AND operator: `field1:value1 AND field2:value2`
- OR operator: `field1:value1 OR field1:value2`
- Parentheses for grouping: `field1:value1 AND (field2:value2 OR field2:value3)`

**Valid Fields:**
- `spfModuleInstanceId`: SPF Module natural instance ID
- `subgraphId`: Subgraph system ID
- `containerId`: Container system ID

**Value Formats:**
- Hexadecimal: `0x7656`
- Decimal: `30294`

**Operators:**
- `AND`: Both conditions must be true
- `OR`: At least one condition must be true
- Parentheses `()`: Group conditions for precedence control

**Examples:**
- Single condition: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656`
- OR operator: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656 OR spfModuleInstanceId:0x7657`
- AND operator: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656 AND subgraphId:0x8978`
- Complex with parentheses: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656 AND (containerId:0x8976 OR containerId:0x9877)`
- Multiple ANDs: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656 AND subgraphId:0x8978 AND containerId:0x8976`
- Multiple ORs: `spfModuleInstanceId:0x7656 OR spfModuleInstanceId:0x7657 OR spfModuleInstanceId:0x7658`

**Note:** Comma-separated values are NOT supported. Use explicit OR operator instead.

- Multiple subsystems (AND): `subsystemId:0x1 AND subsystemId:0x2`
- Complex with parentheses: `subsystemId:0x1 AND (subsystemId:0x2 OR subsystemId:0x3)`

   - Complex structured data grouping related parameters

elements.description:
Array of calibration elements for this Parameter ID.

This array can contain three different types of calibration elements:

**1. ConfigElement (Simple Parameters):**
   - Single configuration values (volume, gain, frequency)
   - Rendered as UI controls like sliders, text boxes, dropdowns

**2. ElementTemplateArray (Parameter Arrays):**
   - Arrays of configuration values of the same type
   - Used for multi-band EQs, filter coefficients, channel gains
   - Contains template defining the structure of each array item

**3. Struct (Grouped Parameters):**
   - Complex structured data grouping related parameters
   - Contains nested elements of any calibration type

systemId.description: Unique system identifier for the ckv

Ckv.description: Array of Calibration Key-Value pairs. Each entry contains key and value information with their respective IDs, names, and system identifiers.

parameters.description: Array of parameter data, one entry per PID. Each entry contains the system identifier, PID, name, description, and the list of calibration elements belonging to that parameter.

type.description: Discriminator field identifying this as a ConfigElement.

name.description: Unique name of the element within its parent scope. Used as the key when reading or writing the parameter value.

value.description: Current value of the element as a string.

dataType.description: Data type of the element value (e.g. UInt32, Int16, Float). Determines how the raw binary value is interpreted.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this element controls or represents. Displayed as a tooltip or label in the UI.

group.description: Logical group this element belongs to. Used to visually cluster related elements together in the UI.

subgroup.description: Optional sub-group within the group for finer-grained UI organization.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the value (e.g. dB, Hz, ms). Displayed alongside the value in the UI for context.

isReadOnly.description: When true, the element value cannot be modified by the user. The UI should render this element in a read-only state.

displayType.description: Hint for how the element should be rendered in the UI. For example: Slider for continuous ranges, DropDown for discrete valid values, CheckBox for boolean flags, TextBox for free-form numeric entry.

policy.description: Visibility and access-control policy for this element. Hidden elements are not shown in the UI. Basic elements are shown in the default view. Advanced elements are shown only in the advanced/expert view.

qFormat.description: Q-format notation string indicating the fixed-point scaling of the value (e.g. Q15 means the value is scaled by 2^15). Used when displayType is QFormattedValue.

precision.description: Number of decimal places to display when rendering the value in the UI. Applies to floating-point and Q-formatted values.

min.description: Minimum allowed value for this element. The UI should prevent the user from entering a value below this bound. Not applicable when dataType is RawData.

max.description: Maximum allowed value for this element. The UI should prevent the user from entering a value above this bound. Not applicable when dataType is RawData.

allowedValues.description: Enumerated set of allowed values the client may choose from. When present, the UI should restrict input to these values only (typically rendered as a DropDown). Each entry may be a NameValuePairDto or BitFieldDto.

linkedElementNames.description: List of element names that are linked to this element. These elements have a relationship with this element, typically through formula calculations. Used by the UI to understand and manage element relationships.

type.description: Discriminator field identifying this as an ElementTemplateArray.

name.description: Unique name of the array element within its parent scope.

isReadOnly.description: When true, none of the array elements can be modified by the user.

template.description: Array of prototype elements defining the structure of each item in the array. Each entry carries the default or definition value as specified in the module definition — not the current calibrated value. May contain a mix of ConfigElement, ElementTemplateArray, and Struct entries.

value.description: Ordered list of concrete element instances in the array. Each item follows the structure defined by the template and may be a ConfigElement, ElementTemplateArray, or Struct.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this array represents.

group.description: Logical group this array belongs to for UI organization.

subgroup.description: Optional sub-group within the group for finer-grained UI organization.

length.description: Fixed number of elements in the array. If absent, the length is determined at runtime by lengthFormula.

lengthFormula.description: Expression evaluated at runtime to determine the array length when the length is not statically known (e.g. "num_channels * 2"). Variables in the formula (like num_channels) are linked to other config elements,

type.description: Discriminator field identifying this as a Struct.

name.description: Unique name of the struct element within its parent scope.

isReadOnly.description: When true, none of the struct elements can be modified by the user.

structType.description: Type identifier for the struct, corresponding to the named struct type in the module definition (e.g. "AudioConfig", "FilterSettings").

value.description: Child elements contained within this struct. May be any mix of ConfigElement, ElementTemplateArray, or Struct.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this struct represents.

group.description: Logical group this struct belongs to for UI organization.

subgroup.description: Optional sub-group within the group for finer-grained UI organization.

type.description: Discriminator identifying this entry as an allowed value option.

name.description: Human-readable name for this allowed value

type.description: Discriminator identifying this entry as a bit field item.

allowedValues.description: Enumerated set of allowed values the client may choose from for this bit field. Example: [{name: "Enable", value: "1"}, {name: "Disable", value: "0"}]
